memory_candidates.content: This codebase has a reusable shared-library pattern for reconciling copy-pasted regex/pattern logic across multiple consumer scripts: scripts/lib/task-reference-patterns.sh is `source`d by both a lint script and a write-time hook, exporting shared pattern variables and helper functions so both consumers are guaranteed to agree byte-for-byte, with a deploy-tree-first/source-store-fallback resolution list and a loud (not silent) failure if the library can't be found. This is the model to follow any time the same regex/pattern needs to be kept in sync across 2+ independently-maintained files in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts and hooks.

plan-format.md's 'Consumer sites of this shape' documentation for the ### Phase N heading contract is itself incomplete/goes stale silently -- a prose-maintained consumer list drifts the same way copy-pasted regexes do. When auditing consumer sites for a documented shared contract, grep for literal usages (e.g. the heading prefix string) across the whole extensions tree rather than trusting the documented list alone; this research found 3 additional files (general-implementation-agent.md, general-implementation-hard-agent.md, commands/task.md) that plan-format.md's own consumer-site paragraph named but a later task's FILE SCOPE omitted.
